answer: Each identity registers in an atlas, locks one bond in a karst vault chamber, and files a fable declaration naming its item. The bond for the k-th identity is 100+10(k-1) credits, so 1,000 fakes lock 5,095,000 credits. Chambers cannot be merged, so one bond cannot back two identities. Any auditor can recompute the ladder from the atlas order and check each chamber and fable appears once; a duplicate fable burns both bonds. A fable reuse ring fails because its second filing is rejected and its bond burns. An honest agent locks one bond and recovers it after a clean epoch.
